Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $32 million class fund, distributed automatically to identified members, plus $2 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval. Any fees the court does not award would augment the class fund. We are open to discussing the fund amount, but an automatic distribution is important given Brightline’s records.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic distribution is appropriate given the available records. To resolve the case promptly, Brightline proposes a $28 million class fund plus $2 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval, with any unawarded fees going to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $28 million class fund with automatic distribution, plus $2 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval, with any unawarded fees going to the class and no clear-sailing provision.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Start with a substantial class recovery reflecting the $64 million in disputed charges, litigation risk, and the delay to trial. Automatic payments are feasible because Brightline has members’ records. Keep fees separate, subject to court approval, and direct any unawarded amount to the class.

The $34 million proposal is within authority and has strong approval prospects, but there is room to negotiate a lower total outlay. Preserve automatic distribution and the fee terms that favor approval while countering on the fund.

The $28 million fund exceeds the estimated $27.5 million trial-value benchmark even before accounting for certification risk, delay, and litigation costs. Automatic distribution benefits all identifiable members, and the fee provisions avoid clear sailing and reversion concerns. Accepting is in the class's interest.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement resulted from negotiations between class counsel and Brightline’s counsel. Because those negotiations were confidential mediation communications, I do not recount the parties’ proposals or exchanges. The agreement provides a $28 million class fund for automatic payments to identified class members, plus $2 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses subject to court approval. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request, and any fees not awarded will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline.
